segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: We're not looking for final recommendations.

segments.speaker: Martin Shelby
segments.text: Then what direction are you Planning on giving?

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: This is what they asked for. They asked for direction on amendment to council rules. They are basically asking our opinion. And after the opinion, we'll have a next step and we'll talk about that. But thank you.

segments.speaker: Martin Shelby
segments.text: Okay. Well, I'm responsible for amending council's rules. I'm not prepared to take direction today.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: I did not say that. I said this is my comment. My comment is that public comment should happen after every one and this is why. That's all I wanted to do was make that statement. I just want my fellow council members to listen because I think we all can hear that today that we didn't get to hear from everybody about the bpac and not going to hear from everybody about this. I'm not going to open public comment for only one thing. That's not fair.

segments.speaker: Martin Shelby
segments.text: Now I understand your point, councilwoman. I thank you for that and accept that. Council's rules are council's rules and they are subject to amendment and change.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: Yes, they are. I want to talk, though, about what you asked for direction on. Amending council rules to establish a timeline for application, I think we go for 45 days. I think making a decision about a number of days is important. I would just go for 45 days. As far as standing members to each board and commission, who gets to decide who is standing? So I'm thinking about my time on the VRB. The VRB has very specific roles. Are we going to say that a builder should get standing? I would disagree with that. We'd have to really be careful about who you approve for standing. Maybe it's something that rotates and that standing is two years or standing is three years. You'd have to have some parameters around that because for the VRB, there is no like open membership. The only ones are neighborhood leaders. I appreciate the neighborhood activists, but I don't necessarily think those should be people with standing either. If you have a commission where every seat has a specified seat, you may need to -- like I said, I would rotate that. As far as the term where the individual boards are consistent with those to the appointing body, I tend to agree. I think more with council member Maniscalco that -- I think we should have them consistent, but also it doesn't have to be changed. The only thing that I would counter with council member Carlson about just having a year is that there is a huge learning curve to these committees. So by the time you are in for a year, you are basically finally getting your feet under you. I might have a time where you discuss with your person, like how is it going? What do you like? Are you interested in staying on? More than just doing one year. Removal of board members for excessive absence, absolutely a yes for unexcused absences. And I think it should be at three. And I think whatever you need to do to tighten the language, I think you're getting a full thing there. I am really not in favor of noncitizens serving on boards. I think it's really important that you have -- it's really hard to even say if you own property -- well, if you own property, you're still not dealing with most of the stuff that has to do with the city on a daily basis. I really think that's very important. If we had to, my only line would be not just owning property but owning a business. I think you should have to do both. So there has to be some real -- or owning property and being a vested former employee or owning a business and being a vested -- I think you should have two. If we came up with three or four ways, you should have to have two of those. I think the connection to the city has to be incredibly strong and has to be something where you are in the city every day. I think that's just really critical. We have 400,000 people in the city. If we could get people to serve on boards and commissions when we had a hundred thousand, I think the biggest problem is we don't do a very good job in advertising. We don't push this out to civic organizations. We should be pushing it out to every possible group. We have so many people that volunteer in the city for so many different things. I really believe that people just don't know that they can serve on a board and/or they don't know that they are qualified. They feel like it is this big thing. And for half of these boards, it's not a qualification issue. So let's do a better job at getting some numbers out before we go outside of the 400,000 people who already live here. Councilman Miranda, I saw your light pop on?

segments.speaker: Charlie Miranda
segments.text: I agree with mostly everything you said, along with everyone that spoke, the three before me. I think they have some good things. The terms about board members, if you are not here, then they got to leave, you know, I don't think so. Let's say we appoint somebody now and some of us are not here and after March, does that mean that individual, he or she is out of the board automatically?

segments.speaker: Dana Crosby Collier
segments.text: In response to your question, if you appoint someone for the remainder of your term and they do the orientation and they never come back, then your question is, would they be automatically out in march? They would remove -- under the perfect-world scenario, they would continue to serve until their replacement is confirmed. So your successor then or you, whoever is sitting in the seat in March, would then appoint someone else. Because now it's a new term. A new council member term. But they wouldn't automatically just drop --

segments.speaker: Charlie Miranda
segments.text: We don't do it for anything else. Do we?

segments.speaker: Dana Crosby Collier
segments.text: No. if --

segments.speaker: Charlie Miranda
segments.text: I understand what you're saying. Let me put it the other way. If that rule stands, the incoming person, whoever he or she is, can still have that person?

segments.speaker: Dana Crosby Collier
segments.text: Yes, they would still have their seat until they are removed.

segments.speaker: Charlie Miranda
segments.text: Unless you put it in writing.

segments.speaker: Dana Crosby Collier
segments.text: Yes. Unless we tweak the enabling ordinance to allow them to be removed.

segments.speaker: Charlie Miranda
segments.text: I understand.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: Yeah, I would tend to agree with Councilman Miranda. Somebody needs to be in there for a little bit and then maybe get to know that person and see if there is somebody else you would want. Okay. My second request is going to be that you reach out to the three council members who are unavailable today and make sure you get their answers to this question. And then what will happen is I will ask you to reach out to the chair to set this on a subsequent meeting just because I don't know what's going to happen. I know the chair is on it, so I'm not concerned at all. This will be a moment, though, for public comment. So now that we are finished with this -- and this is why. I really do appreciate the idea of brevity but I think it kind of ruins the entire point of a workshop if we can't hear from -- I might make that motion tonight, but I might make that motion next week to reconsider these rules because I don't think they are serving the purpose they are supposed to serve. If anybody wishes to speak on public comment for items 3 and 4, please come up and we would be happy to hear from you. I see I have one person. I think the other two might be just listening. If not, they can come up as well. Ms. Poynor, I love your shirt. It's not as fun from the front until you read the back. [ laughter ] I've had it for a long time. Now you are on tv. Anyway, I had it a long time. I kept forgetting to wear it. Good morning, Stephanie poynor. Every single committee and this needs to be written into the rules, needs a babysitter. They have to have somebody who guides them through the process. They don't have a babysitter, then they are wandering aimlessly. The budget committee when I started in 2021, we had several babysitters over time. We are pretty settled in now. I would agree that the first year on a committee, I mean the first year on the budget committee, I probably didn't say boo, not much at all because it's so complicated and so complex. I'm very concerned that the only reason that we're talking about taking somebody off of a committee or a board is attendance. Because we all know that you have people who are on committees now who are not representing you as a board. They are not doing what you would do as a group consistently. That's not okay. If there's somebody who is not doing what they are supposed to be doing, what if their behavior is inappropriate? What -- there's nothing that says you can remove somebody. You guys have already been through that with the Planning Commission. You had to have legal look into if you could dismiss somebody from the Planning Commission. If you don't put anything in there, then there's no way to do it. I also have screamed bloody murder because the whole concept of shoving people in there for three or four years when the person who is putting them there is not going to be around in three or four years, that's not appropriate. And it should be -- I mean, I don't think it should happen instantaneously, but appointments to committees, everybody can renew somebody. They can keep them on. There's nothing that says that you have to fire somebody when you leave. As a matter of fact, Councilwoman Hurtak, when she came on board, I contacted her because I was councilman dingfelder's appointee. What do you want to do? She said I'm good for now. We'll leave it alone. Never had a conversation since. It was her personal decision to keep me on. I think that's the way it should be. The new person should have that opportunity to replace them with their person. There's been lots of turnover on council, so there's been lots of turnover on the budget committee. I would also like to say, if you're going to put a former employee on a committee, that that person needs to have some knowledge and some foundation for that particular committee, not just willy-nilly they worked for the city so they must know everything. What I found over time is that the people who worked for the city are very myopic about their own personal jobs, and they don't know the breadth of everything that everybody else in the city does. So don't just automatically put somebody in for this. You know, I really have an issue because I have things to say about the bike stuff.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: Which is why I made the comment. It sounds like we have agreement here. Thank you. Joseph Citro, 33611 for the record. Agenda item number 3. Councilman Carlson, I live on Bayshore. I hear you loud and clear. We have a problem. Every day this city's population doubles from people coming in from pinellas, polk, pasco, hernando, sarasota, manatee. If we can alleviate some of that traffic on our roads, we can make our roads safer. We have four members of this council that belong to the mpo/tpo of Hillsborough county. Please, use your voices so we can get better public mass transportation. Councilman Carlson, all fatalities, pedestrian fatalities that have happened on Bayshore is because people were breaking the law. Speeding, driving drunk, driving under the influence of drugs. I learned from a very wise transportation planner, expert that our bike lanes are not safe until we have some sort of physical barrier, whether it be a parking lane where cars separate themselves from traffic flows to the bike lanes. Or a concrete barrier, maybe 8 inches tall. People do not ride in the bike lanes because they are scared to be there. Barriers are needed to make those bike lanes safer. But we have a growing problem. We have sidewalks that are now being infiltrated by e-vehicles. We're not using human-powered vehicles, whether it be scooters, bikes, monowheels, skateboards on sidewalks, and those are endangering pedestrians. We have e-bikes that are now going 30, 40 miles an hour on sidewalks. People are scared to walk on sidewalks now. Agenda item number 4. Three and a half years ago, I personally signed up for a board. I've been on Civil Service Board, Variance Review Board, Code Enforcement board, charter review board. And somebody whose ego was too big. There was only six positions. Six people were there, including myself, to be on that board. Somebody's ego was so big that they decided not to appoint me to that board. To the presenters, first statement, we don't have enough people to fill the boards. It would have been my pleasure to serve on that board for three years. Again, council member's ego was too big. Madam chair, board, thank you.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: Thank you very much. Anyone else for public comment? I think we'll hold new business until evening, if that's okay.

segments.speaker: Guido Maniscalco
segments.text: I want to make a comment, not new business. We know victor dimaio and the dimaio family, his mother mercy passed away. I know she worked for the city. She was involved in I don't know how many boards over the years. And victor's father, victor senior, legendary guy, always giving back to the community, run for office, served on boards, they have done it all. And I want to offer my condolences to the family. Like I told victor, your mother lived a full lifetimes ten. Because my whole life growing up, she was involved in Ybor City, West Tampa, the city, you name IT. Services are going to be tomorrow -- or there is a wake, I believe, at 4:00 at boza and roel on Armenia for those who wish to attend. She lived a good life. She gave back endlessly to this community. My condolences to the family. That's it.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: Anyone else? Okay. Well, then we are adjourned until 5:01 --

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: Motion to receive and file by council member Maniscalco, second from Councilman Miranda. All those in favor? Aye. Any opposed?
